notes: Load profiling starts before the five-map lifecycle load and ends after two server ticks.
Teardown profiling covers bottom-up deletion of the five Bush maps.
The load, topology, and whole teardown wall-clock values are single host runs and are not used as stable improvement ratios.
Both raw captures passed all hard five-map, depth, teardown, profiler, viewer, and PVS lifecycle gates.

change.topology: Map removal first resolves the owning Z-network from the removed map component, retaining the prior network enumeration only as a stale-index recovery path. The topology event now identifies a rebuilt network versus a removed map and includes the affected map and depth.
change.roof: Initial network construction retains the full top-down roof rebuild. Map removal seeds roof state from surviving higher maps and writes only levels below the removed depth; removing a lowest remaining map performs no roof traversal or writes.
change.power: A topology event queues only the affected Z-network reactor power group. Existing MapInit APC/receiver area refreshes are preserved; no visibility, power-domain, reactor, or scheduling cap was added.

roof.conclusion: The required initial roof behavior and work counts are unchanged. The single-run timing difference is not claimed as an improvement.

power.conclusion: The measured 0.1284 ms global enumeration was redundant because all 1,221 APC/receiver updates were already pending from MapInit. The after capture removes that enumeration while preserving the 1,221 legitimate area updates. The wider wrapper timings are single-run host measurements and are not used as stable improvement ratios.

bottomUpTeardown.conclusion: Bottom-up deletion cannot affect roofs on any surviving lower level, so all four broad rebuilds were eliminated. Map ownership resolved directly in all five removals. This result does not imply that removing a middle or upper level performs no roof work.

validation.releaseBenchmarksBuild: Passed with zero warnings and zero errors.

focusedIntegrationTests.behavior: The lifecycle test creates aligned lower and middle floor tiles, verifies that the middle level roofs the lower level, removes the middle map, and verifies that the lower roof contribution is cleared.

deferredRisks: The Bush initialization capture had no reactor-powered-light entities. The targeted group refresh preserves the existing whole-query light implementation, but a populated reactor-light topology mutation still needs live coverage.

The initial 20,095-tile roof rebuild remains synchronous and allocated approximately 323 KB. Its work is required for initial roof state, and one sample does not justify caching, capping, or scheduling it differently.

Removing a middle or upper map still traverses surviving maps above it to seed roof state and rewrites affected maps below it. The focused integration test proves behavior, but the synthetic two-tile case is not a large burst benchmark.
Bulk mapping edits and znetwork-variantize were not exercised; per-tile propagation during those workflows remains MZ-014 follow-up work.
All levels intentionally retain the existing shared RMC Z-network power domain. This change does not resolve the MZ-064 gameplay-policy question.
The paired captures are deterministic headless host runs, not live-round scheduling or network captures.
